issues.display_title: Issue #1080: Continue with GoThru: sign in to Floormap through Keycloak (realm gothru)
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Add Continue with GoThru to Floormap's login and register pages: sign in through GoThru's central Keycloak (realm gothru), following the GoThru SSO strategy deck (2026-08-27) and the integration contract in GoThruMedia/gothru-sso docs/gothru-sso-integration-guide.md. Floormap is not among the deck's participating apps yet (Gothru, Panorra, Villume, Tour Mkr) — this task makes it one.

Why: the goal is importing panoramas straight from the user's own TourMkr tours instead of pasting a tour link into Add Panorama. That picker needs the user's GoThru identity; this login is the first step. The picker is a follow-up task.

Keycloak clients (from the SSO admin, 2026-09-21)

value
Realm gothru — production Keycloak https://id.gothru.org (discovery live, PKCE S256)
Client (development) floormap-dev — origin https://mapthru-dev.xyrus10.dev
Client (production) floormap — origin https://map-thru.com
API audience gothru-api (the access token's aud)
Redirect URI <origin>/callback
Library keycloak-js — it builds the login URL itself

So the client is public (no secret), driven from the browser like Panorra's.

What exists (checked 2026-09-21)

Piece State
Floormap auth NextAuth 5.0.0-beta.31, Credentials + Google (src/auth.ts). Google's id_token is swapped for a Go-issued session JWT at POST /v1/auth/google in the signIn callback.
keycloak-js ❌ not a dependency yet — added by this task (^26.2.4, Apache-2.0, no dependencies; approved)
Floormap Go API ❌ no Keycloak support — backend counterpart: GoThruMedia/Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#182
GoThru API (GoThru-API-New) ✅ already accepts Keycloak: POST /v1/auth/keycloak-login, users.keycloak_sub. Not used by this task — it is what the tour picker will call.

Scope

  1. Button. "Continue with GoThru" next to "Continue with Google" on /login and /register, keeping redirectTo. keycloak-js (pkceMethod: "S256", checkLoginIframe: false) sends the browser to Keycloak with redirectUri = <origin>/callback. keycloak-js is loaded on demand, not shipped to every login-page visitor.
  2. /callback page. keycloak-js finishes the code exchange (PKCE, public client) and yields the access token; the page hands it to a NextAuth credentials provider gothru, whose authorize sends { "access_token": … } to POST /v1/auth/keycloak (BE task) — the guide's backend contract, same as Panorra — and returns the Go session like the email/password provider does. The Floormap user id stays the Go user's UUID, not the Keycloak sub.
  3. Only when configured. Button and provider exist only when NEXT_PUBLIC_GOTHRU_SSO_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_GOTHRU_SSO_CLIENT_ID are set (realm defaults to gothru). None of them is a secret.
  4. CSP. keycloak-js POSTs the code to the realm's token endpoint from the browser, so the SSO origin joins connect-src (derived from the env, like Countly). No iframe, so frame-src stays closed.
  5. Existing methods stay. Email/password and Google keep working unchanged.

Out of scope

  • Tour picker in Add Panorama (follow-up: GoThru /v1/auth/keycloak-login → GET /v1/tours/list → tour_key → existing processTour).
  • Global logout (Keycloak end-session). Floormap's Log out stays local: the GoThru SSO session survives, so the next Continue with GoThru returns without a password — the deck's "local logout".
  • Silent sign-in without a click (check-sso) — the deck leaves this open.
  • Linked Accounts screen in Profile.

Dependencies

  • Redirect URI <origin>/callback and web origin <origin> on both clients — floormap: https://map-thru.com; floormap-dev: https://mapthru-dev.xyrus10.dev. Verified 2026-09-21 against id.gothru.org: both authorize requests reach the login form (an unregistered example.com/callback is rejected), the token endpoint answers both origins with Access-Control-Allow-Origin + Allow-Credentials: true (an unknown origin gets 403), and a public-client token request gets invalid_grant, not invalid_client — no secret required. localhost:6060 is not registered: local GoThru sign-in goes through the dev tunnel URL.
  • Dev client id is floormap-dev (floorma--dev → "Client not found").
  • FE env: NEXT_PUBLIC_GOTHRU_SSO_URL=https://id.gothru.org, NEXT_PUBLIC_GOTHRU_SSO_CLIENT_ID (floormap-dev in dev .env.local, floormap in env.prod). Baked in at build — env.prod only once BE #182 is live, or the button leads to a refused exchange.
  • BE endpoint merged and deployed.

Open questions (product)

  1. Account matching. Plan: match on keycloak_sub, then on a verified email (and link the sub), otherwise create the account — the same as Floormap's Google login and GoThru API's keycloak-login today. The deck says "never merge accounts on email alone"; the integration guide allows the verified-email link "only if the product has approved this behavior". Is it approved for Floormap?
  2. Wording and logo. The deck mixes "Gothru" / "GoThru" / "Go thru" and two different logos. Which one goes on the button?

Acceptance criteria

  • /login and /register show Continue with GoThru when the SSO env is set, and hide it when not.
  • Clicking it opens the GoThru Keycloak login; after signing in the user comes back through /callback and lands on redirectTo (dashboard by default) with a working session (projects load, /v1/auth/me answers).
  • With an active GoThru SSO session (already signed in to another GoThru app), Continue with GoThru signs in without asking for credentials.
  • An existing Floormap user with the same verified email lands in their existing account with their projects, not a new empty one (subject to open question 1).
  • Email/password and Google login behave exactly as before.
  • A refused exchange (BE 401/5xx) or a failed callback lands on /login?error=… with no session.
  • No token in URLs, logs or storage beyond the callback; no CSP violations.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

Source: GoThru SSO strategy deck ("Continue with Gothru — Central Identity & Single Sign-On", 2026-08-27).

RESULT

Merged to development in PR #1081 (caf9852, commit 36798c0). Dormant until the env is set: without NEXT_PUBLIC_GOTHRU_SSO_URL + NEXT_PUBLIC_GOTHRU_SSO_CLIENT_ID, neither the button nor the provider exists.

How it works (per the SSO admin's client setup and the gothru-sso integration guide):

  • The button loads keycloak-js on demand and sends the browser to id.gothru.org (public client, PKCE S256, redirectUri = <origin>/callback, no login-status iframe).
  • /callback (src/app/(auth)/callback/): keycloak-js finishes the code exchange. The access token goes to the NextAuth credentials provider gothru, which posts { access_token } to POST /v1/auth/keycloak (BE #182) and returns the Go session.
  • The Google exchange moved into src/lib/auth/providerSignIn.ts, shared with GoThru. The SSO origin joins CSP connect-src.
  • New dependency: keycloak-js ^26.2.4.

Also fixed: a Google sign-in the Go API refused landed on Auth.js's bare /api/auth/error 403 page (AccessDenied is an error-kind failure → pages.error, which was unset). It now returns to /login?error=.

Verified

Check Result
pnpm test / tsc / lint 284 files, 2563 passed / clean / clean
E2E, refused exchange (local OIDC stand-in, real Chrome) public token request with PKCE, backend gets only access_token (aud=gothru-api, azp=floormap-dev) → /login?error=CredentialsSignin
E2E, accepted exchange /login?from=/start → /callback → session with the Go user id → lands on /start
Env unset only Continue with Google; Google still reaches accounts.google.com
Real Keycloak config (id.gothru.org) both clients accept <origin>/callback; CORS + credentials for both origins; public client (invalid_grant, not invalid_client)
CSP violations none

Not verified: a real GoThru sign-in end to end — needs BE #182. Before turning it on: dev .env.local gets NEXT_PUBLIC_GOTHRU_SSO_URL=https://id.gothru.org + NEXT_PUBLIC_GOTHRU_SSO_CLIENT_ID=floormap-dev (sign in through https://mapthru-dev.xyrus10.dev; localhost:6060 is not registered); env.prod gets client floormap once #182 is live.

Open questions 1 (verified-email linking) and 2 (button wording/logo — a neutral key icon for now) are still open.

issues.display_title: Issue #1085: docs(prd): align the Object Layer Order PRD with what shipped (#943)
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Repo: gothru-3d-floormap · docs only, no code change · branch docs/943-layer-order-wording → product-docs (PR #947)

The Object Layer Order PRD and brief (#943, docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-09-07-editor-overlay-object-layer-order/) still contradict what shipped in #953 (released in #954). PR #947 folded the #944 decisions in, but a full read of both files turned up passages it missed, and one behaviour #953 shipped that no document describes.

Decision: the editor's 3D panel (2026-09-22)

ad730ab (part of #953) fixed z-fighting between overlapping shapes of equal height in the editor's 3D panel with a per-shape polygonOffset ordered by array position. It is a depth bias only: height, position, geometry, store, map and export are unchanged. The panel now draws the same shape on top as the 2D plan does, and follows To Front / To Back. #945 and #953 flagged this for PM, and nobody answered.

Accepted: keep ad730ab and change the docs. The editor's 3D panel follows the 2D shape order. Preview, live view, embedded view and map view still show no visible change.

Scope

  1. 3D panel. Reword every passage that promises no change to the 3D view:
    • PRD: Non-goal 1, R11, the acceptance checklist, QA scenario 8, Risk 1.
    • Brief: the Proposed Solution paragraph, In Scope 7, Out of Scope 5, Success criterion 8.
  2. Ordering is within one type (D1=B). Two passages still read as cross-type: PRD Goal 1 ("above or below another supported visual object") and the brief's Hypothesis ("above or below another object").
  3. R11 vs R14. R11 "affects only the 2D editor canvas" conflicts with R14, because the All list order changes. The same goes for brief In Scope 7 ("2D editor canvas only"). Scope becomes the 2D canvas, the sidebar lists, and the editor's 3D panel for overlapping shapes.
  4. Undocumented, user-visible changes from #953.
    • Fallback row names for points, safety markers, access markers and shapes now number by age, not by array position. In tie groups the numbers change once, on the first load after release; a bulk panorama import is one such group.
    • Viewers get no three-dot menu. The edit affordance is removed, not disabled.
  5. Housekeeping. QA scenarios have two items numbered "3."; renumber them. Move R13/R14 below R12.

Out of scope

  • Any code change. ad730ab stays as shipped.
  • The map's own coplanar shape overlap (lib/map/geojson-utils.ts). #953 noted it as a possible separate task.
  • Editing #943's body. It is the source issue.

Acceptance criteria

  • Neither file promises "no visible change" to the editor's 3D panel. Preview, live, embed and map keep that promise.
  • Neither file implies ordering across types.
  • R11 and brief In Scope 7 agree with R14.
  • The age-based row numbering (with its one-time renumber) and the viewer rule are stated.
  • QA scenarios are numbered 1..12 with no duplicates, and requirements run R1..R16 in order.
  • Committed on docs/943-layer-order-wording. Push waits for approval.

Source: PR #947 review · PRD #943 · Decisions #944 · Implementation #945 / #953

RESULT

Commit 5b22b25 on docs/943-layer-order-wording (PR #947 → product-docs). Docs only, no code change. prd.md +54/−14, brief.md +10/−6.

  • 3D panel: new 3D panel section. It says overlapping equal-height shapes stack in layer order, as a render-only tie-break, accepted 2026-09-22. Non-goal 1, the checklist, the QA scenarios, Risk 1, and the brief's Proposed Solution / In Scope 7 / Out of Scope 5 / Success 8 now keep "no visible change" to preview, live, embed and map only.
  • Same-type ordering: PRD Goal 1 and the brief's Hypothesis now say "of the same type".
  • R11 now covers the 2D canvas, the sidebar lists and 3D panel stacking, so it agrees with R14. Brief In Scope 7 matches.
  • Documented the rest of what #953 shipped: a Row names section (fallback numbers by creation order, and a one-time renumber in tie groups such as a bulk panorama import) and a Who sees the menu section. These are also R15 / R16, two checklist items, QA scenarios 8–10, and Risk 4.
  • Housekeeping: QA scenarios are renumbered 1..12 and requirements run R1..R16 in order.

Checked against main: LayerOrderMenu returns null for !canEdit, and objectRows numbers every reorderable type by age (numberByAgeById, tie on id).

Not pushed yet. Push waits for approval.

issues.display_title: Issue #1086: Logout is slow when clicked while the dashboard is loading
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Problem

Signing out from the dashboard sometimes takes several seconds before the sign-in page appears.

Measured on the dev app (click Logout → /login form visible):

When Time Server actions before /login
Logout while the dashboard is still loading 5.0 / 5.8 / 9.2 s 5, one after another
Logout after the dashboard has settled 2.1 s (x3) 1

Root cause

  1. Logout waits behind the dashboard's data requests. logoutAction() is a server action, and Next runs server actions one at a time. Opening the dashboard fires four of them (loadMe, listRecentProjects, listProjects twice). A logout clicked during that time only starts after all four finish, each 0.4–3.7 s. Navigations are not queued this way.
  2. The click is held up by a re-render. useUserStore.setUser(null) runs before the action and re-renders the whole project grid (useDashboard.ts ownership filter, ProjectViews.tsx owner label), about 600 ms of main-thread work in dev.
  3. Sequential round trips. The /login fetch starts only after the action returns. From outside the server network each request to production takes about 0.3–1.3 s.

The same flow is used by the sign-out button on /verify-email-pending.

Scope

  1. Add POST /api/logout, a route handler that calls signOut({ redirect: false }).
  2. Dashboard Logout and the verify-email-pending sign-out call it with a plain fetch, then navigate (/login and /register), so logout no longer waits behind pending dashboard actions.
  3. Clear the cached user after navigation starts, so the re-render no longer delays the request.
  4. Keep the sign_out analytics event queued before the session ends.

Out of scope

  • Server or network latency to production.
  • Signing out of GoThru / Keycloak.

Acceptance criteria

  • Logout clicked while the dashboard is still loading reaches /login without waiting for the dashboard's requests.
  • Logout sends exactly one request before /login loads.
  • After logout, /dashboard redirects to /login (session cookie cleared).
  • The verify-email-pending sign-out still lands on /register, signed out.
  • The next sign-in does not show the previous user's name.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit pass.

RESULT

Root cause: logout was a server action. Next runs server actions one at a time, so a logout clicked during the dashboard's initial load queued behind getMeAction, listRecentProjects, listProjects and getBannerAdAction. Separately, the next-auth auth() proxy wrapper re-sets the session cookie on every proxied request, so a dashboard action already in flight could bring the session back after logout.

Fix (PR #1088, merge 332167f, commit 6002269):

  • src/app/api/logout/route.ts: POST /api/logout route handler replaces logoutAction. It is outside the action queue.
  • src/lib/auth/signOut.ts: requestSignOut(), used by DashboardNav and verify-email-pending.
  • src/lib/auth/sessionCookie.ts + src/proxy.ts: proxy responses no longer re-issue the session cookie. The session still rolls through /api/auth/session.
  • DashboardNav: navigates to /login before clearing the user store, so the project grid doesn't re-render first.

Measured (dev): click 1.5 s after load 3.9–6.8 s → 0.6–0.8 s; click at load 7.1–24.2 s → 0.6–1.5 s; session cleared 5/5.

Known edge: a logout clicked before the page's first /api/auth/session response comes back (about one round trip) can still get the session back. Closing it fully needs server-side token revocation.
Not browser-tested: sign-out from verify-email-pending.

The slow dashboard load itself is #1087.

issues.display_title: Issue #1087: Dashboard initial load runs its four server actions one after another
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-1087-one-request.mp4

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Problem

Opening the dashboard fires four server actions, and they run one after another instead of together. From outside the server network every request to production costs about 0.3–1.3 s, so the dashboard waits for four round trips plus four backend calls before the project list is complete.

Found while measuring #1086 (logout waited behind these same actions).

What happens today

On mount the dashboard calls:

Action Caller
getMeAction loadMe(true) in useDashboard.ts load()
listRecentProjects useDashboard.ts load()
listProjects useDashboard.ts load()
getBannerAdAction GoThruBanner.tsx

load() wraps the first three in Promise.all, but Next runs server actions one at a time, so Promise.all has no effect: each action starts only when the previous one returns. Measured on the dev app, each took 0.4–3.7 s (backend through the dev tunnel), and the four together finished 3–6 s after the page loaded. Any action the user triggers meanwhile (publish toggle, duplicate, delete, filter change) waits behind them too.

Scope

  1. Load the dashboard's initial data in one round trip, e.g. one server action that fetches the profile, recent projects and the project list in parallel on the server, or plain fetch to route handlers, which are not serialised.
  2. Keep the banner ad from delaying the project list.
  3. Keep today's behaviour: loadMe(true) still refreshes the shared user record (#273), the "not authenticated" error still sends the user to /login, and the error/retry state still works.

Out of scope

  • Backend response times.
  • Filter/search/sort refetches after the initial load.

Acceptance criteria

  • Opening the dashboard sends at most two requests for its initial data (project data + banner), not four sequential ones.
  • Profile, recent projects, project list and counts render as they do today.
  • A signed-out or expired session still redirects to /login.
  • An action clicked right after opening the dashboard no longer waits for the initial load.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit pass.

RESULT

Fix (PR #1089, merge 5eb8485, commit 496d452):

  • src/actions/projects.ts: getDashboardBootstrapAction runs getMeAction, listRecentProjects and listProjects side by side on the server, in one action (same pattern as getEditorBootstrapAction, #1031). It returns failure as { ok: false, reason: "unauthenticated" | "failed" }, so an expired session still goes to /login in production builds, where a thrown action error's message is replaced.
  • src/app/dashboard/useDashboard.ts: load() uses it, sets the user store on every load (#273 refresh kept), and keeps the error + retry path.
  • src/app/api/banner-ad/route.ts + GoThruBanner.tsx: the banner loads over a route handler, in parallel, outside the action queue. It used to go first in the queue because it mounts before the dashboard's load effect runs.
  • Tests: 3 new in src/actions/__tests__/projects.test.ts (success, 401 → unauthenticated, list 500 → failed).

Measured (dev, 3 runs): data requests on load went from 4 serial actions to 1 action + banner GET in parallel. Project list ready: 7.3 / 8.1 / 10.6 s → 5.3 / 6.3 / 6.1 s. What's left is mostly /v1/projects itself (2.3–6.6 s from this machine).

issues.display_title: Issue #1091: Logout can be undone by a session request still in flight
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Problem

After a logout, the user can end up signed in again. In production (release 4c2f215), logout clicked while the dashboard was still loading brought the session back in 2 of 2 runs: the login form came up, but opening /dashboard afterwards went straight in. The run where Logout was clicked after the dashboard had fully loaded signed out correctly.

Found while checking #1086 in production.

What happens today

Logging out deletes the session cookie (POST /api/logout, #1086). The session is a stateless JWT, though, and every GET /api/auth/session response re-sets that cookie (it keeps the session rolling). A session request sent before the logout that answers after it puts the cookie straight back:

+85122ms  set-cookie SET    GET  /api/auth/session
+85418ms  set-cookie DELETE POST /api/logout
+87256ms  set-cookie SET    GET  /api/auth/session   ← signed in again

The page asks for the session as soon as it hydrates, so the window is however long that request takes. It was about 18 s on the slow link this was measured from, and it is about 1–2.5 s from a normal connection. #1086 closed the same gap for server actions and proxied requests by no longer letting the proxy re-issue the cookie; the session endpoint was left rolling on purpose.

Scope

Make a logout stick on the server, so a cookie that comes back afterwards is no longer accepted:

  • When POST /api/logout runs, record the session it ends. The key is the Go accessToken held in the session JWT: it stays the same for the life of one sign-in. The JWT's own jti can't be used because Auth.js generates a new one on every refresh.
  • The Auth.js jwt callback returns null for a recorded session. Auth.js then treats the request as signed out everywhere it checks: the proxy, server actions (getToken) and /api/auth/session. The last one also clears the cookie.
  • Keep each record until that access token expires (its exp).

In memory, in the Next server process: production runs a single pm2 process (fork mode). Records are lost on restart; a shared store is only needed with more than one instance.

Out of scope

  • Revoking the Go access token itself (Go API contract change).
  • Signing out the user's other devices or sessions.

Acceptance criteria

  • Logout clicked while the dashboard is still loading: opening /dashboard afterwards lands on /login, including when a session request was still in flight at the time of the click.
  • A session cookie saved before logout and replayed afterwards is refused (proxy redirects /dashboard → /login, /api/auth/session returns no session).
  • Signing in again after logout works, including with the same account in the same browser.
  • Other sessions of the same account (other browser/device) stay signed in.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit pass.

RESULT

Fix (PR #1093, merge f83c824, commit fba60a5):

  • src/lib/auth/signedOutSessions.ts: in-memory record of sessions ended by a logout, keyed by the SHA-256 of the Go access token, kept until that token's exp. Stored on globalThis so the proxy and the route handlers (separate bundles, same process) share it.
  • src/app/api/logout/route.ts: records the current session before signOut.
  • src/auth.ts jwtCallback: returns null for a recorded session, so a cookie that comes back is treated as signed out by the proxy, server actions and /api/auth/session (which also clears it).
  • Tests: src/lib/auth/__tests__/signedOutSessions.test.ts (4).

Verified in the browser, with the page's own /api/auth/session response held until after the logout so the production race happens every time:

  • development without the fix: the cookie comes back and stays, /dashboard still opens.
  • this branch, on the dev server and on a standalone production build: the cookie comes back and is cleared about 100 ms later, /dashboard → /login.
  • On both dev and the standalone build, the other acceptance criteria pass too: a replayed pre-logout cookie is refused by the proxy and by /api/auth/session, signing in again in the same browser works, and the same account signed in elsewhere stays signed in.

Limits: records are per process and lost on restart. Production runs one pm2 process; more than one instance needs a shared store.

issues.display_title: Issue #1092: feat(blue-line): Blue Line tours dashboard on mock data
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

First slice of the Blue Line Editor PRD (#1082), front end only, on mock data.

The GoThru API cannot back this feature yet: GET /sv/blueline/list returns nothing but {moderation_id, sequence_id, processing_state} (no tour name, thumbnail, stats_key or owner email), and there is no write endpoint at all for panorama lat/lng/heading. So the list ships against a fixture now, and the fixture is the seam the real client drops into later. This task deliberately stops before the editor — its Save is the part that is blocked.

The UI design (#1083) is already implemented on design/-blue-line-editor: this task integrates that work into development rather than rewriting it.

Scope

  • Blue Line entry in the dashboard sidebar and in the account popover.
  • /dashboard/blueline with the three connection states from the design: not connected, connected but empty, connected with tours.
  • Recent tours strip plus the full tour list, on fixture data.
  • Search over tour name, tour key, Place ID and owner email.
  • Sort: latest edited, earliest edited, name A–Z, name Z–A.
  • Pagination of the full list.
  • Per-tour actions: View Blue Line (https://tourmkr.com/F1{tour_key}), View Stats (https://stats.tourmkr.com/{stats_key}), Share modal.
  • Sync button, resolving against the fixture.
  • /dashboard/blueline/{tourKey}: the map-only editor — tour metadata, panorama list, the link graph over MapLibre, placement tools (move, rotate, scale, reset), map filters and undo/redo, all against the same fixture.

Out of scope

  • Any call to the GoThru API — no tour list, no connect, no sync, no save. The connect, sync and save buttons resolve locally against the fixture.
  • Clone as 3D Project actually creating a project.

Acceptance criteria

  • Blue Line appears in the dashboard sidebar and routes to /dashboard/blueline.
  • All three connection states render and match the design.
  • The tour list shows thumbnail, tour name, tour key, Place ID, owner email and the opened timer for every fixture tour.
  • Search matches on tour name, tour key, Place ID and owner email.
  • All four sort options reorder the list.
  • Pagination pages through the full list.
  • View Blue Line and View Stats open the documented URLs in a new tab.
  • The Share modal shows the share link and the embed option.
  • Opening a tour lands on the map-only editor with its panoramas and links drawn; an unknown tour key 404s.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint and tsc --noEmit are green.

Blocked follow-ups, tracked separately once the API lands: real tour list, GoThru account connection, placement save, clone execution.

Refs #1082, design #1083.

RESULT

Merged to development as 5c81701 (PR #1095, commit 4dd873f).

Integrated the UI design from design/-blue-line-editor (#1083) rather than rewriting it: 19 files, +4336 lines.

Shipped

  • /dashboard/blueline — the three connection states, the Recent strip, and the full list with search (tour name, tour key, Place ID, owner email), the four sorts and pagination.
  • Per-tour actions: View Blue Line (https://tourmkr.com/F1{tour_key}), View Stats (https://stats.tourmkr.com/{stats_key}), Share modal, Clone form.
  • /dashboard/blueline/{tourKey} — the map-only editor: tour metadata, panorama list, the link graph over MapLibre, placement tools and undo/redo.
  • Blue Line joins the account nav through src/lib/navigation/accountRoutes.ts, so DashboardSidebar keeps rendering one list; nav items gained an optional badge for the SV pill.
  • Fixture at src/lib/blueLine/mockTours.ts — the seam the real client drops into once the API exists.

Changed while integrating

Design branch Merged
Fixture at src/mocks/blueLine.ts with a tour-level thumbnailUrl nothing read src/lib/blueLine/mockTours.ts, field dropped — the cards draw a generated SVG
Both pages hardcode the "Support Team" account signed-in user from useUserStore
Unknown tour key falls back to the first fixture tour notFound() — otherwise the wrong tour shows under the right URL
Rotate knob and scale handle mirror their value into local state they read the prop; the parent owns it and clamps scale to 0.5–2.5×, so the copy could drift past the clamp
Marker positions projected inside the effect body first projection on a frame (react-hooks/set-state-in-effect)
DashboardSidebar rewritten (~70 lines) to special-case one item one nav-list entry, ~20 lines

Verification — pnpm test 2576 passed / 3 skipped, pnpm lint clean, tsc --noEmit clean. Walked signed-in in the browser: the three states render, search narrows the list, an unknown tour key returns 404, and the editor draws its six panoramas and their links over the basemap, with no console errors.

Open for QA / product

  1. Blue Line sits under Workspace in the sidebar, following the design branch's own code and the newest list screenshot; R1 and two older screenshots put it under Settings.
  2. The disabled "Settings — Soon" row the design adds to the sidebar is not included — it has no behaviour, and the account popover already carries that notice.
  3. Recent shows three cards, matching the design; R5 asks for four.
  4. No role gating: R6 scopes the list to the signed-in user's own tours, so every signed-in user sees the menu. supportOnly is one flag away if that is wrong.

Still blocked on the GoThru API — the real tour list, connecting a GoThru account, saving placement, and Clone actually creating a project. Connect, Sync and Save resolve against the fixture.

issues.display_title: Issue #1096: fix(blue-line): draw panorama nodes as plain dots on the editor map
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Follow-up to #1092. On the Blue Line editor map, panorama nodes render as circular photosphere chips, and a marker-mode control in the top-right corner switches between photospheres, plain dots and an automatic mode that swaps to dots below zoom 16.5.

The photosphere chips should go. A Blue Line is read as a path of capture points, and a 30 px photo per node crowds that path — Street View itself draws plain dots. The panorama list in the sidebar keeps its thumbnails; this is about the map only.

Scope

  • Panorama nodes on the editor map always render as the blue dot.
  • The photospheres / dots marker-mode toggle disappears with them — there is nothing left to switch between.
  • The sidebar panorama list keeps its thumbnails.

Acceptance criteria

  • No panorama image renders on the editor map at any zoom level.
  • Nodes draw as blue dots, keeping their selected, hover and drag states and the node-id tooltip.
  • The marker-mode control is gone from the map's floating controls; zoom and the rest are untouched.
  • The sidebar panorama list still shows its thumbnails.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint and tsc --noEmit are green.

Refs #1092, #1082.

RESULT

Merged to development as 99c4b58 (PR #1097, commit ee63ba3). One file, src/components/blue-line/editor/BlueLineMapCanvas.tsx.

  • Panorama nodes render as the blue dot at every zoom; selected, hover and drag states and the node-id tooltip are unchanged.
  • The marker-mode control is gone from the map's floating controls — it only switched between photospheres, dots and an automatic mode that swapped to dots below zoom 16.5. Zoom and the other canvas controls are untouched.
  • The sidebar panorama list keeps its thumbnails.

Verification — pnpm test 2580 passed / 3 skipped, pnpm lint clean, tsc --noEmit clean. In the browser on the editor route with the basemap loaded: zero <img> elements inside the map's marker layer, zero photosphere/dots toggle buttons, six sidebar thumbnails still present, no console errors.

issues.display_title: Issue #1099: Share modal shows the current project password
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Source: #1098 · Depends on GoThruMedia/Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#184 (ship the BE first)

Problem

In the Share modal, a secured project only says "A password is set — type a new one to replace it, or leave the field blank to keep it." (src/components/preview/SecuredProjectSection.tsx:114). The owner can't see the password they set, so handing it to a viewer means setting a new one. #1098 asks for it to be viewable.

Scope

  • New server action in src/actions/projects.ts that calls GET /v1/projects/:id/password (API-GO#184) and returns string | null. Answers 404, 403 or a throw also come back as null, so this ships safely ahead of the BE.
  • SecuredProjectSection, which only renders when canManageSecurity in PreviewShareModal:
    • When the project is secured, load the current password and put it in the Project password field, masked by default. The existing eye toggle reveals it.
    • Editing it and Save security replaces it exactly as today, and the new value shows next time the modal opens.
    • The "leave the field blank to keep it" wording no longer fits a field that already holds the password. Reword the note for this state.
  • Password set before the BE change (secured, but the API returns null): keep the field empty. Say the current password can't be shown because it was set before passwords became viewable, and that typing it again (or a new one) makes it viewable.
  • Where the password lives: only in the section's component state. Never in a Zustand store, localStorage or analytics, and don't fetch it for users who can't manage security.

Acceptance criteria

  • Secured project whose password was set after API-GO#184: the field shows it masked, and the eye reveals the exact password.
  • Change it and save, then reopen the modal: the new password shows.
  • Secured project from before API-GO#184: the field is empty and the note explains why and how to make it viewable.
  • Non-secured project: no password request is made; the section behaves as today.
  • A user without canManageSecurity makes no password request.
  • With the BE endpoint missing (404): the modal behaves as today, with no error shown.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit pass.

RESULT

PR #1101, merge 9ce11d4, commit dfbd632. Uses API-GO#184 (PR #185, live on 1.226).

  • getProjectPasswordAction (src/actions/projects.ts): GET /v1/projects/:id/password → string | null. null for not secured, hash-only, 403/404, or a network error, so the modal never errors.
  • SecuredProjectSection:
    • loads the current password into the field when the project is secured, masked until the eye is pressed, and never over typed text
    • the shown value isn't a change (Save stays disabled); an edited password saves and stays shown
    • a hash-only password keeps the field empty, with a note on how to make it viewable
  • Tests: 6 new in SecuredProjectSection.test.tsx, 4 in projects.test.ts. pnpm test (2591), lint and tsc pass.
  • Browser check on a scratch published project, deleted afterwards:
    • set a password, save, reopen: the field holds it masked, and Save is disabled
    • the eye reveals it
    • unlock with it gives 200 + grant; a wrong one gives 401
